open_release.rationale: The paper frames synthetic populations as public use files and shareable replacement datasets from confidential data.

quotes.text: The production of synthetic datasets has been proposed as a statistical disclosure control solution to generate public use files out of protected data

pipeline_testing.rationale: No testing or format-conformance purpose is stated; the aim is realistic synthetic populations.

ml_augmentation.rationale: The 'augmented datasets' are inputs to micro-simulation models, not training data for predictive models.

statistical_replication.rationale: The paper requires the synthetic population to match marginals and correlation structure and reports a utility assessment against real data.

quotes.text: The performance and acceptability of such a tool relies heavily on the quality of the synthetic populations, i.e., on the statistical similarity between the synthetic and the true population of interest.
We demonstrate the use of simPop by creating a synthetic population of Austria, and report on the utility of the resulting data.

causal_inference.rationale: No causal or structural-model framing appears in the sources.

education.rationale: The paper mentions sharing replacement datasets 'for research or training' and demonstrates the package, but no course or tutorial use is shown.

quotes.text: “replacement datasets” that can be shared as public use files for research or training.

benchmarking.rationale: The full text is truncated and the README is thin; the visible text only describes other tools and does not show simPop used as a baseline.

imbalance_correction.rationale: No minority-class or imbalance framing appears in the sources.
